text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- Britain's Glaxo Wellcome, American Home Products, Poland's Ciech chemical trader and a group of the largest listed Polish banks have bid in the privatisation of drug maker Polfa Poznan.
Germany's Hoechst, Poland's Chemia Polska SA and France's Rhone-Poulenc Rorer seek shares in drug maker Polpharma.
- Brewer Strzelec will increase production from the proceeds of its public offering of 8.2 million shares at a minimum price of 2.3 zlotys from July 14 to 18.
- Eighty percent of foreign firms active in Poland want to increase investment, 13 percent keep it stable and three decrease it, a survey by an industrial and trade foreign investor group said.
HSBC James Capel said in a report that Poland will need to lower its budget deficit to help decrease domestic demand and thereby its trade deficit.
National Investment Fund Zachodni in Poland's mass privatisation programme will likely sign a contract on Wednesday to sell its Centrozlom scrap-metal-processor firm.
Unofficial sources say Stalexport will take a 60-percent stake but neither Stalexport nor the NFI would comment.
In this year's third quarter textile firm Bawelna Silesiana, belonging to NFI Kazimierz Wielki in the NFI programme, will enter Poland's regulated over-the-counter market.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
